live_test: Audited live 2026-09-20 (S6). Asked the layer for its own totals: 51,308 rows in all, 3,360 with LANDUSE='Multi-Family', newest multi-family ISSUED 2026-09-17 -- the feed is live, not frozen. The old where clause (TYPE='New' only) returned 168 rows whose newest permit was 2026-06-12; that is genuinely all TYPE='New' multi-family holds (max ISSUED for that exact filter is also 2026-06-12), so nothing was being lost to paging or a bad URL. The gap was the type list: this layer also carries TYPE='New Commercial', which holds 117 multi-family rows (116 since 2024-09-01, newest 2026-07-16) that TYPE='New' never saw. Adding it brings in two real new apartment projects the run was missing -- 'San Marcos Student Housing / Lindsey St Apartments' at 419/420 North St and 435 N Comanche St (issued 2026-07-16; independently confirmed as the McLain student-housing development approved by San Marcos council at Lindsey and North St, raised to seven storeys) and 'The Heritage at Cottonwood Creek Multi-Family' at 4530 Hwy 123 Bldg 1 (issued 2026-02-24, 37,491 sq ft). TYPE='New Residential' holds zero multi-family rows. Both queries return exceededTransferLimit=false, so no paging is needed.
notes: This layer's granularity is per building-unit/per-permit, not per-project -- e.g. '3810 TRANSPORTATION WAY APT 301/303/304/329' are separate rows for one building. Measured live on 2026-09-20 after adding TYPE='New Commercial': 284 matching rows, 1 aged out, and merge_records collapsed the feed to 8 projects. That ratio is still 'suspect' because 161 rows are single units inside ONE building (3810 Transportation Way, The Village at Centerpoint Station), while the new commercial type adds three building rows for San Marcos Student Housing / Lindsey St Apartments and one row for The Heritage at Cottonwood Creek. So the remaining suspect flag here is mostly per-unit granularity, not paging or a frozen feed -- San Marcos genuinely has only a handful of distinct new apartment projects, which is what a city of ~72,000 should look like. There is still no aggregate unit-count field on this layer, so units stay None ('Units: not public yet') and are never estimated from row count -- though the per-unit rows do imply a real count (161 distinct APT numbers at 3810 Transportation Way), recorded as a finding. SQUAREFEET is a per-unit floor area here (680-1,476 sq ft), so it must not be shown as a building size; that is why it stays unmapped. LANDUSE='Multi-Family' is the closest verified real apartment filter; there is no apartment-only sub-code. 'Townhouse' and 'Duplex' are separate LANDUSE values and hold no new rows since 2024-09-01.
